title: Protocol for the setup and use of a human choroid plexus endothelial-epithelial two-cell-type in vitro model
protocol: Place a 12-well plate into a sterile, stainless steel box for surgical instruments.
Place the 12-well plate containing filter inserts into a sterile stainless steel box for surgical instruments.
Use sterile forceps to place the filter insert into the 12-well plate.
Fill the filter insert with HIBCPP medium using sterile forceps.
Turn the filter insert upside down within the HIBCPP medium to avoid air bubbles getting into the filter compartment.
Aspirate additional medium until the well is filled halfway.
Place a drop of medium on the filter membrane to pre-wet the membrane.
Place stainless steel box at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Add HIBCPP cell suspension to filter membrane in stainless steel box.
Incubate filters for 24 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Flip filters into a 24-well plate in correct orientation after incubation.
Start the experiment with inversely flipped and medium-filled filter inserts.
Place insert in correct orientation in a 12-well plate using sterile forceps.
Fill insert with HIBCPP medium using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Fill the entire well with HIBCPP medium.
Flip the insert “under water” to prevent air entry.
Remove medium until well is approximately half filled.
Pipette 8 × 10^4 HIBCPP cells (80 μL of cell suspension adjusted to 1 × 10^6/mL) onto the bottom side of an inverted and medium-filled filter insert.
Pre-wet the top side of a 0.4 μm pore size filter insert with some extra HIBCPP medium before seeding cells.
Incubate the seeded filter inserts for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Remove remaining medium from the top of the insert before pipetting the cell suspension onto the filter membrane.
Cover the seeded filter inserts with the lid and incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 (v/v) for 24 hours.
Turn the filter inserts to the standard orientation into a 24-well plate containing 1 mL HIBCPP medium per well after day one.
Add 500 μL HIBCPP medium into the upper compartment of the filter insert.
Prepare iHCPEnC solution with 1 × 10^5/mL cells when TEER values reach approximately 100–200 Ω cm² (usually 4 days after seeding).
Add 4 × 10^4 iHCPEnC to the upper compartment of the filter insert containing HIBCPP medium.
Measure TEER every day for the next 4–5 days.
Pre-warm 4% and 8% PFA in PBS to 37°C.
Prepare a well with 1 mL 4% PFA in PBS for each insert to fix.
Start with the fixation of the endothelial cell layer.
Carefully remove 250 μL of medium from the upper reservoir.
Slowly add 250 μL of pre-warmed 8% PFA in PBS for a final concentration of 4% PFA.
Fix iHCPEnC for 20 min at room temperature.
Transfer every insert to its 4% PFA well and fix HIBCPP cells for 20 min at room temperature.
Stop the fixation step by gently washing twice with PBS at room temperature.
Cut out the membrane of the filter insert with a scalpel.
Place the membrane on a 50 μL drop PBS.
Lift the membrane with forceps from the PBS drop and place it in a 50 μL drop of 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS.
Submerge the membrane for 5 min to permeabilize the cells.
Wash the cells by placing the membrane in the next drop containing 50 μL PBS.
Repeat the washing step.
Pipette a 50 μL drop of 2% BSA in PBS on the strip of ParafilmR and submerge the membrane to block the cells for 15 min at room temperature.
Prepare a further 50 μL drop of 2% BSA in PBS containing the primary antibody at the desired dilution.
Incubate the membranes for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Wash the cells twice with PBS.
Prepare a 50 μL drop of 2% BSA in PBS containing the secondary antibody at the desired dilution and DAPI at a final concentration of 1:10,000.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Wash cells once with ddH2O.
Aspirate the remaining fluid and let the membranes air dry for 2–3 minutes.
Place a drop of mounting medium on one side of the cover glass.
Position the filter membrane onto the drop of mounting medium.
Add mounting medium to the other side of the membranes to ensure coverage from both sides.
Mount up to eight membranes within two microscope cover glasses with ProLong antifade mounting medium.
Store overnight (∼24 hours) at room temperature in dark before analyzing the membranes using a fluorescent microscope.
